NO. 039 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Charadriidae · Plovers

Grey Plover

灰斑鸻 · huī bān héng Pluvialis squatarola
Winter visitor Common 27–30 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The big plover that shows black armpits in flight

In winter it is plain grey and white and easy to overlook on a mudflat. But the moment it takes off, that tuft of black under the wing is revealed — the Grey Plover's signature, and nobody else's.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • AxillariesIn flight the axillaries — under the wing, close to the body — are conspicuously black. The most distinctive and most reliable feature of the species.
  • PlumageIn non-breeding dress the upperparts are grey-brown finely spangled with white and the underparts white, with pale grey-brown mottling at the sides of the breast; in breeding dress it is boldly black and white, with a black face and breast.
  • BillStout and relatively short, black, suited to pecking at the surface of a mudflat.
  • SizeMuch larger than Kentish Plover, heavily built, with a relatively large head.

Behaviour

Feeds in the classic run–stop–peck rhythm and often mixes with other waders. In winter its grey and white plumage matches the mudflat so closely that you usually notice it only when it moves. A winter visitor in South China, on coastal mudflats and estuary sandbars.

Voice

A clear three-note whistle, 'pee-u-wee', the middle note slightly lower, often given in the air or on take-off.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Jinwan tidal flats
  • Qi'ao Island beaches
  • Hengqin shore
  • Doumen tidal flats
Field note
See a grey-white, thickset plover out on the mud? Wait for it to fly — one glimpse of black under the wing settles it.
